Variants.Content: Northern society is shaped by cold, distance, old gods, family crypts and memories of long winters. Northerners often regard straightforwardness, keeping promises, hospitality, and preparation for the winter as practical virtues; they know that southern etiquette can obscure interests, and they also know that a distant castle Reinforcements may not arrive in the snow. The nobles in the north value blood and ancestors, while ordinary people are more concerned about whether firewood, granaries, livestock and roads can survive the winter. It is not that there are no plots in the North, but plots usually have to be implemented through family, land and survival needs.
